[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Algorithmic Thinking and Pseudocode"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to Problem Solving in Computer Science"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before writing a single line of code in languages like Python, JavaScript, or C++, a developer must solve the core problem logically. Algorithmic thinking is the foundational skill of breaking down complex problems into manageable, sequential steps that a computer can execute."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"What is an Algorithm?"},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"An algorithm is a finite sequence of well-defined, computer-implementable instructions, typically to solve a class of specific problems or to perform a computation. Every good algorithm possesses the following characteristics:"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Finiteness: The algorithm must always terminate after a finite number of steps."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Definiteness: Each step must be precisely defined; the actions to be carried out must be rigorously and unambiguously specified for each case."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Input: An algorithm has zero or more inputs, taken from a specified set of objects."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Output: An algorithm has one or more outputs, which have a specified relation to the inputs."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Effectiveness: All operations to be performed must be sufficiently basic that they can be done, exactly and in finite length, by a person using pencil and paper."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"The Role of Pseudocode"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Pseudocode is an artificial and informal language that helps programmers develop algorithms. It is designed to be human-readable, bypassing strict syntax rules of programming languages so you can focus entirely on the logic."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Example: Finding the Maximum Value in an Array"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Let us examine how to translate algorithmic thinking into pseudocode for finding the largest number in a list of integers."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"FUNCTION findMaximum(arr)
    IF length of arr == 0 THEN
        RETURN null
    END IF

    SET maxVal TO arr[0]
    
    FOR EACH item IN arr DO
        IF item > maxVal THEN
            SET maxVal TO item
        END IF
    END FOR

    RETURN maxVal
END FUNCTION"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Writing Pseudocode"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Keep statements independent and language-agnostic."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use standard control flow keywords like IF, ELSE, WHILE, FOR, and RETURN in uppercase to distinguish them from variables."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Indent blocks of code clearly to show scope and nesting."},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"By mastering algorithmic thinking and drafting robust pseudocode, you will significantly reduce debugging time and build scalable mental models for complex software engineering challenges."}]
